The test image shows a tomato leaf with multiple small-to-medium brown/necrotic spots scattered across the surface, some with yellow halos. The leaf is otherwise green. Key candidates: Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato, Septoria_Leaf_Blotch, Early_Blight, Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus.

Let me view one reference from each of my top 4 candidates:

**Analysis of test image**: A tomato leaf with multiple scattered small-to-medium brown spots, some appearing to have lighter/tan centers with darker borders and slight yellow halos. No concentric rings, no white powder, no wilting.

**Comparing references**:
- **Bacterial_Speck**: Dark/black, irregular small spots with yellow halos — somewhat similar distribution but spots are darker and less structured
- **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch**: Circular spots with lighter gray-tan centers and darker margins — matches the spot morphology (distinct border + lighter center) seen in test image well
- **Early_Blight**: Larger spots with concentric target rings — doesn't match (test spots are smaller, no rings)
- **TSWV**: Whole-plant bronzing/wilting — doesn't match discrete leaf spots

The test image spots show the characteristic lighter centers with distinct darker borders most consistent with Septoria Leaf Blotch. The distribution (numerous, scattered spots across an otherwise green leaf) also fits.
